notes_context:
These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0005] Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc: In ledgerly, normalize every incoming datetime with `ensure_utc` from `ledgerly.clock` before comparing or doing arithmetic (see `current_period` in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py`).
  (learned from task E03 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
  WARNING: learned on version 1.0.0, this checkout is 2.0.0. Check CHANGELOG.md before relying on it.
- [at-0001] Round money only with round_money: Always round monetary results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 1 passed, 1 failed)
  WARNING: learned on version 1.0.0, this checkout is 2.0.0. Check CHANGELOG.md before relying on it.
- [at-0010] Define rates as module-level Decimal constants: Express rates and fixed fees as module-level Decimal constants (e.g. RATE = Decimal("0.029")) rather than inline floats, so fee math stays exact.
  (learned from task S01 on ledgerly 2.0.0; relied on 1x, 1 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0002] Convert line prices with to_money and ZERO: In ledgerly/invoice.py, wrap raw line prices with to_money() and accumulate sums starting from the ZERO constant imported from ledgerly.money, as line_total and invoice_total do.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
  WARNING: learned on version 1.0.0, this checkout is 2.0.0. Check CHANGELOG.md before relying on it.
- [at-0003] Raise BillingError with stable snake_case codes: Reject invalid input by raising `BillingError` from `ledgerly.errors` with a snake_case code such as `invalid_state`, `invalid_quantity`, `negative_amount` or `invalid_amount`, and pass the offending value as the message.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 6x, 4 passed, 1 failed)
- [at-0004] Exclude bool when validating integers: When validating an integer argument, explicitly reject `bool` first (`isinstance(quantity, bool)`) because `True`/`False` pass `isinstance(x, int)` in Python.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 1x, 1 passed, 0 failed)
  WARNING: learned on version 1.0.0, this checkout is 2.0.0. Check CHANGELOG.md before relying on it.

candidate.title: Round money only via round_money
candidate.content: Never round monetary values with Python's built-in round or Decimal.quantize; use ledgerly.money.round_money (and to_money to coerce inputs), which implements finance policy FIN-2026-07 banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN).
candidate.evidence_quote:
finance policy FIN-2026-07 switches all monetary rounding to
  banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`)
